seoTitle: How to Use the Asana Integration in Slack
metaDescription: Learn how to connect Asana to Slack in 2026, turning channel messages into tasks and receiving status alerts without leaving your workspace.
intro: Constantly switching between Slack and Asana breaks focus, and the official integration solves that by letting you create and manage tasks directly inside your channels. This guide covers installing the app, authenticating your account, and turning conversations into structured, trackable work.

steps.heading: Install the app from the Slack directory
steps.body: Browse the Slack App Directory and add the official Asana integration to your workspace.

steps.heading: Authenticate your account
steps.body: Grant permissions through the secure OAuth connection panel to link your Asana profile.

steps.heading: Link your project dashboards
steps.body: Connect specific active Asana projects so tasks created from Slack land in the right place.

steps.heading: Use slash commands and message shortcuts
steps.body: Create and assign tasks quickly with slash commands, or turn any channel message into an Asana task using the message actions shortcut menu.

steps.heading: Set up channel notifications
steps.body: Configure automated notifications for task completions, comments, and status changes so your channel stays updated.

faq.question: Can I turn any Slack message into an Asana task?
faq.answer: Yes, the shortcut menu on any message lets you convert it into a task or subtask without retyping the content.

faq.question: Do task updates from Asana appear back in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, once notifications are configured, task completions, comments, and status changes can post into the linked channel.

faq.question: Is the Slack-Asana integration free?
faq.answer: Installing the integration is free, though creating and assigning tasks still relies on your existing Asana account plan.

faq.question: Can I change a task's due date directly from a Slack thread?
faq.answer: Yes, task previews inside Slack let you interact with details like due dates without opening Asana separately.
